correctness.rationale: At Walsh level k the squared mass of e_u-e_v is 4/2^d times the number of k-subsets meeting the differing coordinates oddly. For each interior k, take k-1 coordinates avoiding a fixed differing coordinate and a fixed agreeing coordinate, then append either of those two: the parity flips, so the mass is positive. Level zero is inactive and level d is active exactly for odd r. Decompose into the span of the nonzero level projections and the orthogonal remainders of the old eigenspaces. The former has one simple updated root between each pair of active levels and one above the last by secular monotonicity; none lies at an active pole. The interior remainders have dimension binom(d,k)-1>0. For odd r this gives d retained values and d disjoint new values. For even r only the inactive top level can coincide with a new root (zero cannot); substituting 2d into the secular equation gives one strictly positive weight, at which precisely one pair coalesces. For r=2, integrating (1+x)^(d-2) from zero to one gives the claimed reciprocal weight. For instance d=3 and r=2 give active masses 1,1, and their two updated unshifted levels at t=4/3 are 8/3 and 6, the latter colliding with the old top. The identity shift leaves the count unchanged and ensures positive definiteness. The CG conclusion follows from the relative minimal polynomial on a right-hand side with every eigenspace component nonzero: its degree is exactly the distinct count.
residual_risks: No antipodal, negative-weight or multiple-edge claim; no finite-precision runtime, tolerance, or conditioning claim.
